items.name: HL · Error alerts
items.what: The central error workflow: when any connected workflow fails on an automatic run, it sends Tolu a Telegram alert naming the workflow, node, error, time and run link (with an optional Incidents sheet log, switched off).
setup: In Telegram, message @BotFather, send /newbot, name it (for example Harvest Lane Alerts) and copy the token. Send your new bot any message.
Create a Telegram API credential called "Telegram alerts bot" with that token and select it in the Telegram alert node.

Open https://api.telegram.org/bot<TOKEN>/getUpdates in your browser (your token in place of <TOKEN>), find "chat":{"id": and replace YOUR_TELEGRAM_CHAT_ID in Telegram alert with that number. Don't save or share that address.

Optional (Gold mission): create an Incidents tab (time, workflow, node, message, url, cause, fix, minutes_to_resolve), select a Google Sheets OAuth2 credential in Incidents sheet, replace YOUR_SHEET_ID, and re-enable that node.
Save the workflow (it doesn't need publishing). Then in every Harvest Lane workflow open Settings, set Error workflow to HL · Error alerts, and save.
Give every node that calls an outside service Retry On Fail: 3 tries, 2,000 ms apart.
items.test: Import HL · Alarm test, set its error workflow to HL · Error alerts, publish it and wait a minute: your phone shows an alert starting with HL · Alarm test failed, Node: Stop and Error, Error: Test alarm: if you can read this, alerts work, with an Open link to the run. Clicking Execute on a broken workflow will not trigger it; that's expected.

walk.title: Build it: Harvest Lane's alarm system
walk.sample: HL · Alarm test fails on purpose at the Stop and Error node: "Test alarm: if you can read this, alerts work."

steps.say: First, a Telegram bot. Message BotFather, create Harvest Lane Alerts, and keep the token like a password. Send your bot a hello so it's allowed to message you.
This workflow starts with the Error Trigger. Whenever an automatic run of a connected workflow fails, n8n starts it and hands over the details.
show: Receives: execution { id, url, error, lastNodeExecuted }

steps.say: Edit Fields formats the alert. The details live under execution and workflow, not at the top. Pointing at the wrong place is how alerts end up saying undefined.
steps.data: HL · Alarm test · Stop and Error

steps.say: The question marks and fallbacks keep the alert useful even when the failure happens in a trigger and the data has a different shape.
steps.data: Test alarm: if you can read this…

steps.say: Telegram sends Tolu the workflow, node, error, time, and a link straight to the failed run, so diagnosis starts with one tap.
Find your chat ID from the getUpdates address in your browser, but never save that address in a workflow. It contains your token.
An optional Incidents log is switched off for now. Turn it on later for the Gold mission, to track causes and fixes.
show: time, workflow, node, message, url, cause, fix

steps.say: Save it. Then open every Harvest Lane workflow's settings and choose this as its error workflow. One alarm for everything.
show: Each workflow › Settings › Error workflow: HL · Error alerts

steps.say: Add Retry On Fail to every node that calls an outside service, so short blips that fix themselves never wake Tolu.
Prove it with a real failure. Manual runs don't trigger error workflows, so the alarm test fails on a schedule, every minute. Publish it, check your phone, then unpublish it straight away.
show: HL · Alarm test: Every minute → Stop and Error

walk.end: Publish the alarm test, read the alert on your phone, tap the link to the run, and unpublish it immediately.

items.name: HL · Alarm test
items.what: A deliberate failure every minute (Stop and Error) to prove the error workflow reaches your phone from a real automatic run.
setup: Import and save HL · Error alerts first.
In this workflow open Settings, set Error workflow to HL · Error alerts, and save.
Publish it only for the test, and unpublish it as soon as the alert arrives.
items.test: Publish, wait about one minute and check Telegram for the alert, then unpublish straight away. Executions shows one failed run per minute while it is published.
